title: Regular local algebras with separable residue field are adically formally smooth
statement: Let $k$ be a field, and let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $K=A/\mathfrak m$. Suppose that $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and that $K/k$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (every finitely generated intermediate field is separably generated). Then $k\to A$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Neither $A$ nor $K/k$ is assumed to be of finite type, and $A$ need not be complete.

source.place: Tag 07EJ, lemma-regular-implies-fs (statement and proof); invoked in Tag 07EL, theorem-regular-fs, characteristic-zero case and the final positive-characteristic lifting argument.

proof.text: Put $B=\widehat A$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB$. The completion-regularity theorem makes $B$ Noetherian local and regular with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. Since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, the completion modulo ideal theorem makes $B$ complete for $\mathfrak n$ and identifies $B/\mathfrak n$ with $K$ as $k$-algebras. In particular its residue extension is the given separable $K/k$.

source.place: Tag 07EJ, lemma-regular-implies-fs, first paragraph; Tag 07ED, lemma-formally-smooth-completion.

proof.text: The field-lifting lemma makes $K$ formally smooth over $k$ for the zero ideal, by the definition of adic formal smoothness. Apply the complete-target lifting theorem with source $K$, source ideal $0$, target $B$, and $I=J=\mathfrak n$, to the identity $K\to B/\mathfrak n=K$. Here $J^1\subseteq I$, $\bigcap_{a\ge1}(J+I^a)=\mathfrak n$, and the source zero ideal maps to $0=q(I)$. Obtain a $k$-algebra section $s:K\to B$ of the residue map.

source.place: Tag 0C34, lemma-lift-residue-field, proof; Tag 07EJ, coefficient-compatible coordinates via Tag 0C35.

proof.text: By the definition of regular local ring choose $d=\dim B$ generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathfrak n$. Apply the existing complete regular coefficient-coordinate theorem with coefficient field $K$ and section $s$. It gives an isomorphism $\theta:K[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, taking $T_i$ to $t_i$. It is a $k$-algebra isomorphism since $s$ is $k$-linear, and it identifies the variable ideal $V=(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$ with $\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 0C35, lemma-power-series-over-residue-field; algebra.tex Tag 0C0S, lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field, clause (2) and its proof.

proof.text:
We verify adic smoothness of $P=K[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$ explicitly. Take a $k$-algebra $D$, $J^2=0$, and $g:P	o D/J$ with $g(V^r)=0$, $r\ge1$. Lift $g|_K$ to $a:K	o D$ by the field-lifting lemma, and choose $b_i\in D$ reducing to $g(T_i)$. Put $H=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)$. Every degree-$r$ monomial in the $b_i$ maps to zero, so $H^r\subseteq J$ and $H^{2r}=0$. Thus $D$ is $H$-adically complete: all quotients from exponent $2r$ onward equal $D$. Power-series evaluation with coefficients $a$ and variables $b_i$ gives a $k$-algebra map $f:P	o D$. For $F=\sum c_
u T^
u$, its image is the finite sum $\sum_{|
u|<2r}a(c_
u)b^
u$. Reducing this sum gives $g(F)$: the discarded tail lies in $V^{2r}$ and every monomial of degree at least $r$ maps to zero. Therefore $qf=g$. This proves the required lifting property for $P$, and composing maps with $	heta$ and $	heta^{-1}$ gives it for $B$ and $\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 07EJ, second paragraph: coefficient lifting, polynomial lifting, and completion. The evaluation formulation writes their composite on every power series; compare Tag 07NL, lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, proof.

proof.text: Finally take any test $g:A\to D/J$ killing $\mathfrak m^r$. It factors through $A/\mathfrak m^r$. The completion modulo powers theorem identifies this quotient with $B/\mathfrak m^rB$, with its canonical map from $A$. Hence $g$ extends to $\widehat g:B\to D/J$ killing $\mathfrak n^r=(\mathfrak mB)^r=\mathfrak m^rB$. Step 4 lifts $\widehat g$ to $B\to D$; restricting along $A\to B$ lifts $g$. This is precisely formal smoothness of $k\to A$ for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology.
